Chrysler Corporation. Chrysler stated that it is essential that NHTSA take into account the effect that more stringent exhaust emission requirements have on a manufacturer's ability to comply with a fuel economy standard. Decreasing the HC, CO, and NOx requirements from 2.0/20/3.1 to 1.7/18/2.3 will reduce fuel economy by the additional 5 percent. Chrysler analyzed three recalibrated 19<sup>77</sup> passenger car certification vehicles from the 1.5/15/2.0 level to the 1.5/15/3.1 level to demonstrate the negative fuel economy effect of the lower NOx level. They concluded that reducing nonpassenger exhaust emission standards from 2.0/20/3.1 to 1.7/18/2.3 will result in a 5 percent fuel economy loss.
Ford Motor Company.
Vehicle tests were conducted by Ford to determine if the more stringent Federal MY 1979 emission standard evaluated under the MY 1979 test procedures, would cause a fuel economy penalty with the emissions control technology planned for MY 1979. After conducting an accelerated vehicle development program that included the three highest volume light truck engines, Ford concluded that an additional loss of 2 percent (0.4 mpg) was caused by the more stringent MY 1979 Federal emission standard.
